clue.text: Setter recovered from the 'hood

indicators.note: read as re-covered, the letters are wrapped up again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, all six letters

explanation.surface: The crossword setter has been rescued from a rough urban neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is just six letters to rearrange; 'recovered' hides its re-covered reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'hood, short for neighbourhood, means the local urban area, as does the street in phrases like street culture.

clue.text: Omit 26, it's used on piste

parts.note: to skip something is to leave it out
the answer to 26-down, the Spanish cry of approval

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave out a cheer, oddly explained as something done on the ski slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: A number in a clue stands for the answer to that entry, here 26-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier plants a pole in the snow for balance and turning, so it is equipment carried down the slope.

clue.text: Debauchees: artist keeps no records

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

indicators.note: 'no' says the named thing is absent, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A comment that dissolute pleasure-seekers have an artist friend who owns no vinyl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is a word to cut EP out of, leaving KES.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is an old word for a dissolute man of fashion given to drinking and womanising, a debauchee.

clue.text: Reduces intensity of cores of cheapo assets; consults quietly

indicators.note: the core of a thing is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the six
the two central letters of the six
the two central letters of the eight
p, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone scales back reliance on cut-price investments and seeks advice discreetly.
explanation.walkthrough: One 'cores of' serves all three following words, each giving its middle pair of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease up is a phrasal verb for slackening off or lessening effort or pressure.

clue.text: Ranks include first of garrison's fighters

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: tiers are rows or ranks

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: The rows of soldiers include the first of a garrison's troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ranks' suggests soldiers, but here it means tiers, rows stacked one above another.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigers are figuratively fierce combatants, and fighting units and sports teams alike are often called the Tigers.

clue.text: Pyongyang's domain slammed into surrounding well

indicators.note: to surround is to go all around, so one piece encloses another
something slammed is knocked about and bashed out of shape

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
.kp is North Korea's internet domain, and Pyongyang is its capital

explanation.surface: North Korean territory crashes into a well that surrounds it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domain' looks like territory, but it is the internet sense: the two-letter country code at the end of a web address.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkwell is the small pot on a desk that holds ink for dipping pens, so well names it.

clue.text: US actor beheaded uncertain physicist

indicators.note: losing the head means losing the first letter

parts.note: Werner Heisenberg formulated the uncertainty principle

explanation.surface: An American actor has executed a physicist who wasn't sure of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncertain' is not doubt but a nod to the uncertainty principle, which identifies the physicist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesse Eisenberg is an American film actor, known for playing Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Network.

clue.text: Excitedly sourced, having hunted high and low

indicators.note: an excited thing is stirred up, so its letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly tracked down an item after searching everywhere for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sourced' fits the story of finding something, but it is only the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour a place is to search it thoroughly, so having scoured means having searched everywhere.

clue.text: Coffee, Mr Biden?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: American slang for coffee, as in a cup of it
second meaning: the first name of the former US president

explanation.walkthrough: The question reads like offering a drink to the president; both halves name the same three-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup of joe is American slang for coffee, and Joe is the forename of President Biden.

clue.text: After what's taken by Wags, that woman's right about author

indicators.note: 'after' fixes the order, so the later pieces follow the first one

parts.note: wags, jokers, mock people, which British slang calls 'taking the' four-letter shortening of a rhyming-slang name
the possessive pronoun for a woman
R is the abbreviation for right
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Once the footballers' partners have had their say, a woman is proved right about some writer.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs are the wives and girlfriends of footballers, but here wags are jokers, and to take the mick is British for to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Mick Herron is the British novelist behind the Slough House spy series, whose titles fill this grid.

clue.text: Unsettle spirit and fifth columnist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to frighten or unnerve
third meaning: a spy working inside

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two: the verb, the ghost, and the secret agent. A fifth columnist is a traitor working for the enemy from within.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to scare as a verb, and informally both a ghost and an undercover intelligence agent.

clue.text: LS Lowry's detail is obtuse

indicators.note: a detail is a small section cut from a larger painting, so a piece is lifted from within

parts.note: the letters run across the initials and the surname

explanation.surface: An art critic complains that a particular part of an L S Lowry painting is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: L S Lowry was a Manchester painter of matchstick figures; art books print a 'detail', a close-up of part of a canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse can mean slow to understand, dull-witted, which is the slow of a slow pupil.

clue.text: Nags if out of drugs

parts.note: hors is French for outside of, as in hors de combat
Es are ecstasy tablets

explanation.surface: Someone becomes a nag whenever their drug supply runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nags' looks like a verb for pestering; it is the noun for old horses. HORS is borrowed from French, as in hors d'oeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an informal word for a horse, usually an old or worn-out one.

clue.text: Jointly attempt to reverse effort to create nation-state?

parts.note: the prefix co- means together, as in co-author
an invented word: to undo a try, just as undo reverses doing

explanation.surface: Allies together try to undo an attempt to found a new nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: un- reverses a verb, so to untry would be to reverse a try, and co- makes it joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A country is a nation with its own government and territory, the political unit a nation-state describes.

clue.text: 51 on second team

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
taken as written
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A report that fifty-one players are now in the reserve side.
explanation.walkthrough: '51' is not a cross-reference to another clue here; it is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The British and Irish Lions are the touring rugby union side, and many sports teams take the name Lions.

clue.text: Lay ripped to pieces: ready to be sent back

indicators.note: something torn into bits no longer holds its original arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, both words

explanation.surface: A verdict on a poem torn apart by critics: it's fit only to be returned to its author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripped' belongs to the letters as well as starting the signal: the fodder is both words, LAY and RIPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply-paid envelope or card has its return postage already prepaid, so it can be posted back at no cost.

clue.text: Cooking — mine kills — in ovens

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, and to cook something up is to concoct it

parts.note: taken as written, both words

explanation.surface: A warning that my cooking in these ovens is deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' sits happily beside ovens in the surface, which helps it slip by as an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lime kilns are furnaces for burning limestone to make quicklime, so they are industrial ovens.

clue.text: Late Democrat after US leader of the War on Drugs

indicators.note: 'after' fixes the order, putting the first-named piece behind the second

parts.words: US leader of the War on Drugs
parts.note: the Drug Enforcement Administration leads America's fight against drugs
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A deceased Democratic politician succeeds an American drug tsar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' suggests a person or a first letter, but it is the whole agency, the DEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Late describes someone who has recently died, as in the late president.

clue.text: Weapons! — a Republican manuscript

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: Alarm at a Republican document that is all about guns.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark belongs to the definition and helps it read as an outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms is the general word for weapons, as in the right to bear arms or an arms race.

clue.text: Dilettante — in the buff?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dabbler without professional skill
second meaning: an enthusiast, a lover of a pursuit

explanation.walkthrough: 'in the buff' means naked, a false trail; the question mark flags buff read as a fan. The word comes from Latin amator, lover.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur dabbles rather than working professionally, and in the older sense is someone who loves an activity, an enthusiast.

clue.text: Writer of rag denied misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving letters refuse to stay in their proper places

parts.note: taken as written, both words

explanation.surface: A tabloid journalist rejects accusations of bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rag' suggests a trashy newspaper, but it is only letters in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: André Gide was a French novelist and essayist who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1947.

clue.text: Struggling harder — having taken pill, tried again

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within
something struggling is thrashing about, so its letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
E is an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: An athlete struggles more after taking a pill and so has another go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tried' looks like making an attempt; the definition is the courtroom sense of hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that is reheard is heard in court a second time, that is, tried again before a judge.

clue.text: One who determines entry in party or 8

parts.note: a do is a party
taken as written
the answer to 8-down is JOE, an ordinary man

explanation.surface: A bouncer decides who gets into a party.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' stands for the answer to 8-down, JOE, which in turn means a man, as in an ordinary Joe.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman guards the entrance to a club or building and decides who may come in.

clue.text: City where bird entertains new date

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: a loon is a diving bird, the diver
N is the abbreviation for new
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: In some city a woman is out with a fresh romantic partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for a girlfriend, and 'date' plays along, but the bird is the loon.
explanation.definitionFit: London is the capital city of England and the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Spy readies boy to go on the run — one way to get out

indicators.note: to go on is to follow after, so the next piece is placed behind

parts.note: jack is US slang for money, and readies is British slang for cash
a son is a boy
on the lam means on the run
b is bowled, one way a batter is out in cricket

explanation.surface: An agent prepares a boy to flee, as a means of escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'readies' looks like a verb but is the noun for ready cash; 'get out' is cricket, where a batter can be bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackson Lamb is the slovenly head of Slough House, the spy series by Mick Herron.

clue.text: See 9
Is in charge of the French after ribbing upset leaders

indicators.note: 'after' fixes the order, putting the first-named piece behind the second
leaders go in front, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letter of each word
les is French for the, in the plural

explanation.surface: A French official takes charge after mockery unsettles the bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like a reversal or anagram signal, but it is just a word whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule a place is to govern it, to hold power over it and be in charge.

clue.text: Spanish show of approval for Hackney slum?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cheer at a bullfight or flamenco
second meaning: a hole, as a Cockney would say it, dropping the h

explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a district of East London, where the Cockney accent drops the h, so a hole, a squalid dwelling, becomes 'ole.
explanation.definitionFit: Olé is the Spanish cry of approval, and a squalid hovel is a hole, spoken without its h.

clue.text: Bona fide leader, the Sea Admiral at last

indicators.note: at last means at the very end, so only final letters are kept

parts.note: the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: The genuine chief is, finally, the admiral of the seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' tempts you to take a first letter, but it is one of the four words whose last letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fide is Latin for in good faith, meaning genuine, authentic, the real thing.

clue.text: Djokovic's end leads tennis authority to a lesser star

indicators.note: leads are what go at the front, so the opening letters are taken

parts.note: the opening letter of each word
the LTA is the Lawn Tennis Association, the British governing body

explanation.surface: Djokovic's retirement sends the tennis body towards a less famous player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' suggests the last letter of Djokovic, but it is a word in its own right whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars in a constellation are ranked by Greek letter, and delta usually marks the fourth brightest, a minor one.

clue.text: See 23
King is in groin's first waxing

parts.note: R is rex, Latin for king
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A monarch is having his groin waxed for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but it is simply two letters in sequence; 'waxing' is not hair removal but growing, as the moon does.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon is waxing when its visible part grows, so waxing means increasing or rising.

clue.text: Weird kid — but worth a flutter?

parts.note: odd means weird
a son is a child

explanation.surface: An oddball child who might nevertheless be a good bet.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is a small bet in British slang; an odds-on horse is favoured to win.
explanation.definitionFit: An odds-on runner is the likely winner in betting terms, so a sensible target for a wager.
